sentences.text:
Saake Chennaiah, vs The District Collector, on 13 October, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Tarlada Rajasekhar Rao
 Writ Petition No.4336 Of 2013
Order:

This Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for the following relief:-
"... to issue a writ, order or a direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the respondents in dispossessing the petitioner from the land admeasuring Ac.0.98 cents in Survey No.274/2 situated at Tripuranthakam Village and Mandal, Prakasam District and not paying compensation to the said land as being illegal, arbitrary and unreasonable and issue a consequential direction directing the respondents to pay the compensation either to the entire extent of Ac.0.98 cents or to Ac.0.66 cents to the petitioner and release Ac.0.32 cents in the said survey number in favour of the petitioner and pass such other order or orders..."
2.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the respondents.

3. The present writ petition is filed seeking a direction to the respondents to pay the compensation either to the entire extent of Ac.0.98 cents or to Ac.0.66 cents, to the petitioner and to release an extent Ac.0.32 cents in Survey No.274/2 situated at Tripuranthakam Village and Mandal, Prakasam District.

4. The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondents have taken the possession of the land in Survey No. 274/2, illegally and utilized the same without paying any compensation, and the said land was utilized for Nagarjuna Sagar Project, therefore, the State and its instrumentalities cannot deprive a citizen of its valuable property rights without following due process of law and it amounts to clear violation of Article 300-A and Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
5.

The 3rd respondent herein has filed the counter-affidavit denying all the averments made in the affidavit filed in support of the writ petition and would contend that the land required for the purpose of Nagarjuna Sagar Project has been acquired duly by following due procedure under Land Acquisition Act by the then Special Deputy Collector, L.A.Unit, Kurichedu.

6. After filing of the writ petition the Tahsildar has issued a notice dated 21.03.2013 to the petitioner to produce any documentary evidence to show that he is related to Saake Lakshmamma, who is the owner of the property, as per the record, as she has no children, but, till date the petitioner has not produced any documentary evidence or any other evidence to establish his right over the property.
The respondents would contend that the petitioner has acquired the land from one Boya Venkatesh and as alleged in the writ petition that the land was not inherited through Smt. Saake Lakshmamma,

sentences.text: Now, the petitioner is claiming right over the property, while, the respondents are denying the same.
All these facts have to be adjudicated before the appropriate forum, not before this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

8. The disputed question of fact is that the writ petitioner is claiming compensation for the land in Survey No.274/2 and the respondents would submit that the said amount was already paid to original owner.
The petitioner herein has not produced 2007 (6) SCC 186 any documentary evidence to establish that he is legal heir of Saake Lakshmamma, who is the original owner of the property, as per the record.
9. These are all disputed question of facts, hence, this Court cannot adjudicate the said issue under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
If at all the petitioner is aggrieved, the petitioner has to address his concern and the petitioner must submit the required paper work to the relevant forum for his grievance.
Accordingly, the Writ Petition is dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.
